doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Casuals, The Composer club and Bill Evans
summary: Bar mitzvahs and weddings paid the rent; he led groups at The Composer where Bill Evans was intermission pianist.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Meanwhile, while you’re doing this recording, what kind of — are you living in New York City?
And what kind of work was paying your rent?
I mean was there enough jazz gigs around for you to live on it?

Well not primarily jazz, I guess they were casuals, you know like the bar mitzvahs, the weddings, some of those things. I did have a small group, I don’t know what year it was, several groups at a club called The Composer, I don’t know if you ever heard of that room. And I once had Teddy Kotick on bass and guess who the intermission pianist was?
He was the intermission pianist and I says who’s this guy, wow, he really plays you know. I saw him later. I just remember him, Bill Evans was the intermission pianist at
